summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with embedded firmware experience on STM32 microcontrollers: bare-metal C, FreeRTOS, and peripheral configuration across GPIO, timers, ADC, I2C, and UART. Designed custom PCBs in EAGLE (schematic and board layout) and drove hardware/software integration on robotics builds.

Embedded Firmware: Peripheral configuration (GPIO, TIM, ADC, I2C, UART)
Hardware & Test: EAGLE PCB Design (schematic and board layout)

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed, fabricated, and brought up custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed STM32 peripherals directly in bare metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; validated in Proteus.
Built Cortex-M4 microcontroller firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on an STM32 microcontroller; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Debugged and root-caused 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); validated 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware grasping via TCA9548A I2C mux.
Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++; drove five servos with range-gated contact detection.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
